answer: Emission dilution resists sybils: each epoch mints one fixed reward pool shared pro-rata among all attested agents, so creating clones only shrinks every identity slice, the attacker own included. Spawning a thousand fakes never widens the pool; it grinds each share down to a ferrous filing. The payout curve flattens into a ridge rather than a climb, so capital that might wander into identity farms earns nothing extra. Attacker cost: real compute and stake per clone for a strictly diluted, near-zero marginal reward.
